quick_notes.title: Ettuthokai (8 Anthologies)
quick_notes.detail: 1. Natrinai. 2. Kurunthokai. 3. Akananuru. 4. Purananuru. 5. Pathitrupathu. 6. Kalithokai. 7. Aingurunuru. 8. Paripaadal. Note : Purananuru and Pathitrupathu are PURAM (History/War). Paripaadal is both Akam and Puram. Others are AKAM (Love).
quick_notes.explanation: Ettuthokai, which means the Eight Anthologies, is a collection of eight ancient Tamil poetry books. These poems were written over 2,000 years ago during the Sangam period, a time of great literary gatherings in South India. The eight books are: 1. Natrinai, 2. Kurunthokai, 3. Akananuru, 4. Purananuru, 5. Pathitrupathu, 6. Kalithokai, 7. Aingurunuru, and 8. Paripaadal. In these poems, the main theme is called Akam, which means love and personal emotions, or Puram, which means war, heroism, and public life. Specifically, Purananuru and Pathitrupathu are Puram poems about history and war, while Paripaadal contains both Akam and Puram themes. All the remaining books, including Natrinai, Kurunthokai, Akananuru, Kalithokai, and Aingurunuru, are purely Akam poems focused on love.

quick_notes.title: Pattuppattu (10 Idyls)
quick_notes.detail: Includes: 1. Thirumurugatrupadai (on Lord Murugan). 2. Porunaratrupadai. 3. Sirupanatrupadai. 4. Perumpanatrupadai. 5. Mullaippaattu (shortest). 6. Maduraikanchi (longest). 7. Nedunalvaadai. 8. Kurinchippaattu. 9. Pattinappaalai. 10. Malaipadukadaam.
quick_notes.explanation: Pattuppattu is a collection of ten long poems from the ancient Tamil Sangam literature, which was written between 300 BCE and 300 CE. The word Pattuppattu means "Ten Songs" or "Ten Idyls," and an idyl is a simple, peaceful poem describing country or village life. The first poem in this collection is Thirumurugatrupadai, which is a guide poem that praises Lord Murugan, the Hindu god of war and victory. The shortest poem in the collection is Mullaippaattu, which describes the forest region called Mullai, while the longest poem is Maduraikanchi, which describes the city of Madurai and praises the king who ruled there. The other poems include Porunaratrupadai, a guide for war drummers; Sirupanatrupadai and Perumpanatrupadai, which are guides for traveling minstrels or singers; Nedunalvaadai, which describes the cold winter season; Kurinchippaattu, which describes the mountainous region; Pattinappaalai, which describes a coastal town; and Malaipadukadaam, which describes a mountain waterfall. Each poem is a separate work that gives details about the Tamil landscape, people, and culture during the Sangam period.

quick_notes.title: Atrupadai Literature
quick_notes.detail: A genre where a poet/artist who has received gifts from a king guides another artist to the same king. "Atrupadai" means "showing the way".
quick_notes.explanation: Atrupadai Literature is a type of ancient Tamil poetry. The word Atrupadai means showing the way. In this genre, a poet or artist who has already received generous gifts from a certain king writes a poem that guides another poet or artist to go to that same king for rewards. The first poet describes the king's generosity and the route to reach him. This helped wandering artists find patrons who would support their work.

quick_notes.title: Purananuru (புறநானூறு)
quick_notes.detail: A compilation of 400 songs on external life (War, Kings, Bravery, Charity). It is the "Mirror of Tamil History". Famous line : "Yadhum Oore Yavarum Kelir" (Kaniyan Pungundranar).
quick_notes.explanation: Purananuru is a collection of 400 ancient Tamil poems from the Sangam period, which was a classical age of Tamil literature. These poems focus on external life meaning public life and activities like war, kings, bravery, and charity, as opposed to love and personal emotions. Because it accurately describes the rulers, battles, customs, and generosity of that time, it is often called the Mirror of Tamil History. One very famous line from this work is "Yadhum Oore Yavarum Kelir" written by the poet Kaniyan Pungundranar, which means "every place is my homeland and all people are my relatives."

quick_notes.title: Pathinen Keelkanakku (Minor 18)
quick_notes.detail: Composed in the post-Sangam (Didactic) period. Mostly focused on morals/ethics. Includes Thirukkural, Naaladiyar, Inna Narpathu, Iniyavai Narpathu.
quick_notes.explanation: Pathinen Keelkanakku, which translates to "The Eighteen Minor Works," is a collection of eighteen ancient Tamil texts composed after the Sangam period, in what is called the Didactic period, meaning a time focused on teaching lessons. These texts are mostly about morals and ethics, which are rules for how to live a good and honest life. The most famous text in this collection is the Thirukkural, a book of 1,330 short verses on virtue, wealth, and love. Other important works include Naaladiyar, which has 400 poems on moral conduct, Inna Narpathu, which describes forty things that cause suffering, and Iniyavai Narpathu, which lists forty things that bring happiness. Each of these works is written in simple Tamil to teach everyday people how to behave wisely and kindly.

These works are the primary source for understanding the life, warfare, and love of ancient Tamils. TNPSC frequently asks for the number of songs in a book, the author of specific lines, or the 'Akam vs Puram' classification. This is the scholarly base of Tamil identity.
